title: Cavatine from Semiramis
identity: Rossini, Cavatine from Semiramide, in the J.J. Lispet/Tierolff P21 edition arranged by André Lemarc for alto saxophone and piano. Publisher metadata identifies two pages and a grade-3 label; the opened score preview supplies direct notation evidence.

evidence.claim: Opened Tierolff/J.J. Lispet product page identifies Cavatine from Semiramide, item P21, by Rossini, arranged by André Lemarc; scoring includes soprano or alto saxophone (or trumpet), and publisher identifies a grade-3 category. The linked public two-page preview was separately inspected.

Escalated public retrieval of the publisher-linked two-page preview; visual inspection confirms alto saxophone and piano. The opening is Andante grazioso in 6/8; the saxophone enters after active piano arpeggiation with a rapid high-register slurred run and quasi-recitative gestures. Page 2 includes loud rapid runs with sextuplets and fermatas, then a quieter cantabile line over active arpeggiation. Written range and pitch convention were not determined.

score_observations.observation: The alto saxophone part begins after piano arpeggiation in Andante grazioso 6/8, then enters with a high slurred run and quasi-recitative gestures marked by fermatas/quintuplets. Page 2 has f rapid runs including sextuplets and fermatas, followed by a quieter cantabile line with ornaments over active piano arpeggiation. The two-page preview is not the complete work; no full-range or pitch-convention claim is made.

review_focus: Inference from the inspected pages: coordinate the soloist’s quasi-recitative flexibility and fast subdivisions with the piano’s continuous arpeggiated texture, then contrast the ff run passages with the quieter cantabile section.
collection_flag: A published operatic transcription with ornamented quasi-recitative and cantabile writing visible in the excerpt; no younger-player marketing was confirmed.

score_links.description: Tierolff public score preview, two pages; visually inspected.

gaps: Only two preview pages were inspected; full written range and work-wide demands remain unknown.
